tasks.title: BookmarkTabShape: tighten the notch clamp and cover it with a unit test (MASTER-148)
acceptance: THE CLAMP IS TIGHTENED TO HALF THE HEIGHT. src/DungeonMaster.App/Controls/BookmarkTabShape.cs computes the notch as `Math.Min(NotchDepth, bounds.Height * 0.5)` (or an expression the task shows to be exactly equivalent). At the base :36 reads `var notch = (float)Math.Min(NotchDepth, bounds.Height);` — the architect read the whole 48-line file — which permits `notch == bounds.Height` exactly, the degenerate case the comment at :34-35 says it prevents. `bounds.Height - 1`, the row's other suggestion, is REJECTED and the task must not use it: for `bounds.Height < 1` it yields a NEGATIVE notch, so `path.LineTo((float)bounds.Center.X, bottom - notch)` at :42 places the apex BELOW the bottom edge and inverts the notch into a spike outside the bounds — a worse artefact than the degeneracy being fixed — and `1` is an absolute floor in device-independent units that does not scale with the ribbon. Report the re-derived line and the full expression. ANCHOR RULE: every line number in this criterion was measured at 57b7eba and this session's own edits move it; locate each cited construct by content search in the post-change tree, name the command, and write the re-derived line.

THE COMMENT STILL DESCRIBES THE CODE. The comment at :34-35 ("Never let the notch swallow the whole ribbon — a degenerate path renders as nothing at all, which reads as a missing control rather than a bug") is updated or extended to state the half-height bound and why, so that the comment and the clamp agree.
